title: Local perfect models on one immersed lisse residue stratum
statement: Let X and S be Noetherian schemes, i : S → X an immersion, A a complete Noetherian local ring with unique maximal ideal I, and K a complex of modules over the completed constant ring on X [def-sfb-adic-stratified-perfect-data]. Assume K is locally derived complete and its residue is the comparison pullback of a specified bounded etale A/I-complex C. Assume every cohomology sheaf of C pulled back to S is finite locally constant. Then there is a covering sieve of the final object of S_proet, on each member of which the restriction of K is isomorphic to the restriction of sfbCompletedModel X I P, for a bounded complex P of finite projective A-modules. No global constructibility or choice of a stratification is assumed.

source.place: Lemma 6.6.8 and Proposition 6.6.11, forward direction, with restriction along one immersed stratum.

proof.text: Restrict the completed quotient tower and the Koszul/Roos completion unit along i. Immersion inverse image preserves limits and is exact, so the ring comparison and completion unit restrict canonically. Comparison-pullback coherence identifies the restricted residue with the restriction of C. Transport to coefficient-sized site models; boundedness and finite local constancy pass through the exact equivalences. Over the residue field exact geometric stalks identify the total tensor of every K-flat representative with derived tensor and preserve the fixed cohomological bounds.

Apply adicResidueLissePerfectLift to that complete complex and its bounded lisse finite-Tor residue on S. Transport its covering sieve and slice isomorphisms back through the site equivalence. Canonical constant-section maps and scalar insertion identify its completed finite-projective model with the restriction of sfbCompletedModel X I P: check finite free terms and pass to their idempotent summands. Reverse the order of the finite/projective conjuncts. Empty strata have empty covering sieves.

proof_origin.place: Bhatt--Scholze Lemma 6.6.8 and Proposition 6.6.11, one-stratum application and canonical coefficient transport.

mathlib_searches.query: Adic constructible complexes are stratified locally perfect and form a bounded triangulated subcategory
mathlib_searches.results: No exact match for the project adic predicates or their characterization.

mathlib_searches.query: Locally derived complete objects form a triangulated subcategory and constructible residue complexes are closed under cones
mathlib_searches.results: Eight hits, including ObjectProperty.IsTriangulated, its constructor, DerivedCategory.instIsTriangulated, and triangulated closed extension properties. These provide the categorical assembly API, not the geometric lifting or residue comparison.
mathlib_searches.verdict: Used the triangulated object-property API; no exact geometric statement.

mathlib_searches.results: The existing item is the only declaration of these predicates; the integral specialization assumes different coefficient hypotheses.

from.place: The adic stratified-perfect characterization, separated into its geometric and categorical proof steps.
